newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic grades firm in light volume session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic grades firm in light volume session.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes gained for most grade differentials on Monday, while outright prices declined slightly in what was termed an extremely sluggish session by domestic crude traders.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late around 5 cents lower, putting benchmark U.S. crudes at $19.80-90 a barrel. July WTI/Cushing remained steady with June, leaving the Jun/Jul roll at flat.
The fact Monday was the first trading session for June as the prompt cash grade month kept many players out of the market, either exhausted from last week or waiting to deal.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James firmed around 5 cts to trade above an even differential at 2 and 4 cts over WTI/Cushing, boosted by positioning and worries about possible Nigerian supply disruptions.
"It looked like follow-through from May that we saw last week. We finished at a 15-20 cts premium for May, so the move to positive numbers was not that surprising," said a trader.
Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit was able to restart normal production from Forcados on Monday after reaching agreements with local communities to open flow stations shut over the weekend.
Still, violence in the crude producing Warri region continued amid ethnic clashes.
Nigerian sweet crudes are considered a key competitor of LLS/St. James, and any indication of supply cuts boosts the Louisiana grade differential.
Traders said other grade markets were even more subdued, with sours netting no fresh deals.
June Postings remained at a $1.83 value for most of the afternoon.
